coordinateSpace: anchorX/anchorY, advanceWidth/advanceHeight, padding and faceQuad are CSS px of the @1x texture, with a top-left origin. textureFile2x is the same shell at pixelRatio times the resolution; divide its pixels by pixelRatio to get the same coordinates.

shadowContract.note: Phase 1d: the shadow is a synthetic translucent-black blob, not a Cycles catcher. A lying/upright tile gets a rounded rectangle matching the body's long/short sides: rectScale x the body box, plus rectPaddingPx1x, with a corner radius of cornerRadiusFraction x the short half-axis. The top edge is then trimmed by topTrimPx1x while the bottom/left/right edges stay fixed, so the shadow does not spill above the tile (light from above/behind). A standing/tilted tile keeps a capsule at its base. The shape is filled at core alpha 0.60 and blurred with a separable Gaussian (sigma 12 px for lying, 4 px for standing), so the lying edge is very soft. The review/runtime shadow pass unions overlapping blobs with a per-pixel max so adjacent tiles do not double-darken. The body carries the tile only.

stack.note: A wall column is a stack of two tiles built from the same single shell perspective (Tenhou-style: the perspective does not change down the column even though it physically would). The bottom tier is a face-down wall shell; the top tier is the same shell offset by the published stackStepPx, or the face-up dora shell for a revealed indicator. The stack step is the projected thickness (straight up), not the face grid step.

baseScale.note: Phase 1b decision: the Phase 1 @2x output is the new @1x base. The long axis of the projected tile body is now 104 CSS px at @1x (was 52) and 208 px at @2x, so the board coordinate space doubles in both axes and every consumer must read the new shells.json. Render real pixels at the new resolution; never upscale the Phase 1 textures. The shadow is now a synthetic blob with its own padding and sprite, so the old right/bottom shadow and top/left AO pixel contract no longer applies.

shadow.source: synthetic Gaussian blob from the projected table-contact footprint

rig.integrity: CPU Cycles, fixed seed 0, fixed adaptive threshold and OIDN. Each texture records the sha256 of its decoded RGBA for integrity. Re-render comparison is optional: bake_shells.py --bake --verify-determinism (or --audition --verify-determinism) renders everything twice, but it is not part of the standard bake.
